title: Your NPS Investments Just Got Clearer: New Scheme Names and Risk Tags Coming Soon
description: The pension regulator, PFRDA, has introduced new rules for how NPS investment schemes are named and categorised. This means pension funds must standardise the.

faq.a: PFRDA stands for Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority. It is the main regulatory body that oversees and develops the National Pension System (NPS) in India, setting rules for investments, withdrawals, and overall operations.

faq.q: What is "equity exposure" in an NPS scheme?
faq.a: Equity exposure refers to the percentage of your invested money that is put into company shares (stocks). Higher equity exposure generally means higher potential returns but also higher risk, while lower equity exposure means lower potential returns and lower risk.

faq.q: Do these changes affect government employees in NPS?
faq.a: The new classification and naming rules primarily apply to schemes launched by individual pension funds under the Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF), which are typically chosen by private sector and self-employed individuals. Government sector accounts and their specific schemes (like the 4A schemes) largely operate on their own tracks.

faq.q: Will I be charged for these changes?
faq.a: No, these changes are regulatory in nature and are being implemented by pension funds. There are no direct charges to subscribers for the reclassification or renaming of schemes. However, remember that a new one-time onboarding charge of ₹200 for new PRANs registered through a Point of Presence will apply from October 1, 2026.

faq.q: What if I want to change my scheme after these new rules?
faq.a: You can still change your scheme or pension fund, subject to existing NPS rules. PFRDA allows a maximum of two changes of scheme/Pension Fund requests per financial year per PRAN (Permanent Retirement Account Number).
